title: RLTP Access key material (Access Layer 0.54 sections 9.4, 9.4.1, 9.4.2)
description: The plaintext shapes the adapter produces and accepts under rltp-access@0.54 (Access 11): rltp-access-material/0.25 (the welcome material of Membership section 4, re-welcome/refresh-era material produced after its transition, and the beekem/0.1 key-delivery kind material, 9.4.2), rltp-access-keydist/0.25 (the per-device key distribution a transition commits to, Access 9.4.1/10.1), and, accepted only, the legacy rltp-access-material/0.24. keyState: REQUIRED in rltp-access-material/0.25 — a material object produced after its transition (welcome, re-welcome, refresh, recovery) names the key state its keys belong to (RLTP-ACC-9360, 9362): the oid: of the transition that created it (RLTP-ACC-9262), or, for a state an adapter derives by merging without a transition, the adapter's merge identifier (RLTP-ACC-9264: the multibase multihash over the JCS array, in unsigned bytewise order, of the ids of all transition-created key states it merges, directly or through earlier merges); the epoch number is a counter and never names a key state (RLTP-ACC-7042). The receiver verifies the material against the log's binding of exactly that key state (9362, 10110). FORBIDDEN in rltp-access-keydist/0.25: a keydist object the transition itself commits to carries no keyState, its key state being the committing transition (RLTP-ACC-9362, 3005 — naming it would make the operation id a fixpoint of its own content). rltp-access-material/0.24 without keyState is accepted in the welcome of Membership 0.16 until the companion's pin advances, naming the key state of the most recent transition in the admission's ancestry (RLTP-ACC-11100); the receiver supplies that identifier, the object carries none. Every form carries the registered adapter id (Access 11: linear/0.1, beekem/0.1); keys is owned and CLOSED by the adapter registration (RLTP-ACC-9200, 9360). linear/0.1 carries exactly the content key — every further secret is DERIVED from it (HKDF info rltp/v1/epoch-secret/<genesis digest>), never transported, so the log's contentKeyCommitment authenticates all consensus-relevant material; it cannot merge (9705), so its keyState is always a transition id. beekem/0.1 (experimental, 9.4.2) carries its key operation as bytes; Access 0.54 names no closed keys schema for it, so this transcription closes keys to { op } and is expected to change with the adapter version.

v.description: wire version (Access 11): rltp-access-material/0.25 with keyState, rltp-access-keydist/0.25 without it, rltp-access-material/0.24 (no keyState) accepted in the welcome only (RLTP-ACC-11100)

adapter.description: the registered adapter id (Access 9.4, 11); an unregistered adapter is a new identifier (RLTP-ACC-11040)

epoch.description: the epoch counter of the key state (RLTP-ACC-7040); a counter for views and monotonicity only, never the key state's identifier (7042) — at adoption it MUST equal the recipient's current epoch (10110)

keyState.description: the identifier of the key state the keys belong to (RLTP-ACC-9362): the oid: of the transition that created it (RLTP-ACC-9262), or a merge identifier — the multibase multihash (u… base64url or z… base58btc, sha2-256) over the JCS array of the ids of the transition-created key states merged, directly or through earlier merges (RLTP-ACC-9264). REQUIRED in rltp-access-material/0.25, FORBIDDEN in rltp-access-keydist/0.25 and in rltp-access-material/0.24 (RLTP-ACC-9362, 11100). For the key-delivery kind material (beekem/0.1) the helper's current key state (RLTP-ACC-9897); the receiver checks it is the current key state of its own materialization, a historical one only to open history (9898, 10110)

allOf.description: material produced after its transition names its key state (RLTP-ACC-9362)
a keydist object the transition commits to carries no keyState; its key state is the committing transition (RLTP-ACC-9362, 3005)
legacy 0.24 material carries no keyState; accepted in the welcome as naming the key state of the most recent transition in the admission's ancestry (RLTP-ACC-11100)

contentKey.description: base64url (unpadded) 32-byte AES-256 content key; its commitment is the multihash over the raw 32 bytes (Access 7.1); the per-epoch secret is derived, never transported

keyState.description: linear/0.1 cannot merge: every key state is the content key of one transition, named by that transition's id (RLTP-ACC-9705)

op.description: base64url (unpadded) bytes of the adapter's key operation (Access 9.4.2, RLTP-ACC-9870, 9890), addressed to the material's recipient; an enforcement operation's keyOpDigest is the multibase multihash over exactly the key-operation bytes. In the key-delivery kind material (RLTP-ACC-9897) it is a key operation freshly produced by the helper's device at the key state named in keyState that gives the requesting device a leaf or path there; the receiver checks that it applies to that key state under the adapter's rules and MUST NOT compare it with the keyOpDigest of any earlier operation (RLTP-ACC-9898). Transcription placeholder: Access 0.54 names no closed keys schema for beekem/0.1
